title: Modern Full-Stack & React Mastery
description: Test your grasp of modern TypeScript, React hooks lifecycle, CSS layout mechanics, and HTTP REST API architecture.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between `useMemo` and `useCallback` in React?
questions.codeSnippet:
const memoizedValue = useMemo(() => computeExpensiveValue(a, b), [a, b]);
const memoizedCallback = useCallback(() => doSomething(a, b), [a, b]);
options: useMemo memoizes the computed return value of a function, while useCallback memoizes the function reference itself.
useCallback can only be used with asynchronous operations, whereas useMemo is strictly synchronous.
useMemo executes on every single render regardless of dependency changes.
There is no difference; useCallback is simply legacy syntax for useMemo.
questions.explanation: `useMemo` invokes the provided function and caches its calculated result, while `useCallback` caches the actual callback function instance to prevent unnecessary re-renders in memoized child components.

questions.question: In TypeScript, what does the `unknown` type represent compared to `any`?
options: `unknown` is type-safe because you must perform type narrowing or assertion before operating on it, whereas `any` disables all type checks.
`unknown` can only hold `null` or `undefined` values.
`any` is strictly type-checked at compile time, while `unknown` is evaluated only at runtime.
`unknown` is deprecated in modern TypeScript and replaced by `never`.
questions.explanation: `unknown` is the type-safe counterpart of `any`. Any value can be assigned to `unknown`, but TypeScript will not allow operations on it without prior type narrowing (such as `typeof`, `instanceof`, or custom type guards).

questions.question: Which HTTP status code should be returned when a client makes a request with valid authentication but lacks authorization permissions to access the resource?
options: 403 Forbidden
401 Unauthorized
404 Not Found
422 Unprocessable Entity
questions.explanation: `401 Unauthorized` specifically indicates missing or invalid authentication credentials. `403 Forbidden` indicates the server knows who the user is, but the user does not have permission to access the resource.

questions.question: What will be the output of this JavaScript Event Loop snippet?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code logs '1' and '4' first. Microtasks (Promise `.then`) execute immediately after synchronous execution finishes (logging '3'). Macrotasks (`setTimeout`) run in subsequent event loop iterations (logging '2').

questions.question: In CSS Flexbox, what is the default value of the `flex-shrink` property?
options: 1 (items shrink proportionally when needed)
0 (items never shrink)
auto (browser chooses dynamically)
-1 (items invert sizing)
questions.explanation: By default, flex items have `flex-shrink: 1`, allowing them to shrink to fit the flex container when the total width/height exceeds available space.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to mutate React state directly without setter functions (e.g. `state.count = 5`)?
options: React relies on shallow reference equality checks; direct mutation prevents scheduled re-renders and breaks component synchronization.
It triggers a fatal browser memory leak immediately.
JavaScript syntax throws a TypeError when mutating object properties.
Direct mutation bypasses the browser's Garbage Collector.
questions.explanation: React checks whether state object references have changed (shallow equality) to decide whether to re-render. Direct mutation modifies the existing reference in-place, causing React to miss the update.
